Maya (Product): Hey folks — quick sync. Customer 'Pegasus Health' has asked for a private deploy (VPC + on-prem option) with HSM-backed keys, reserved capacity, and an SLO for p95 latency <120ms. They want go/no-go in 2 weeks for a pilot. Need cross-team agreement on scope and launch criteria.
Jonah (Eng Runtime): Thanks Maya. Questions: which model family are they requesting and what's the expected RPS / concurrency? That will affect quantization + kernel targets.
Maya (Product): They're asking for an Llama-3-compatible open family and expect ~20 qps with spikes to 80 for 30m windows. 8 tenants, each ~5 qps steady.
Sarah (Infra): We can reserve a Dedicated pool, but on-prem changes things. For VPC + on-prem hybrid, we need a network design and NAT/fallback path. Also wheel: who owns provisioning for HSM integration?
Lee (Security): HSM + KMS integration is doable but requires a short architecture review and a pen-test signoff for pilot. Need data classification and an audit checklist.
Jonah (Eng Runtime): For Llama-3-ish models at that scale we should target int8 quant + KV cache sharing. Impacts: 1) need model conversion artifacts 2) runtime must expose model-variant fallback to smaller quant profiles. I can prototype a quant profile in ~5 working days.
Anika (Eng SRE): On SLOs: p95 <120ms is tight for on-prem unless we control hardware. Need to define degradation policy: if latency >200ms for 5m, route to Hosted fallback. Also we need observability hooks for token-level latency and prefix cache hit metrics.
Alex (Solutions): I'll own customer-facing acceptance criteria and runbooks. Can someone draft an acceptance checklist? Quick list from me: onboarding script, integration test hitting KMS/HSM, load test (20->80 qps spike), failover exercise to Hosted, and a security signoff.
Maya (Product): Perfect. Can we capture minimal Launch Criteria now so product can commit to customer date?
Jonah (Eng Runtime): Draft Launch Criteria (WIP):
```
- Runtime supports quantized model artifact (int8) for customer model
- KV/prefix cache enabled and observed cache hit >= 30% under steady load
- Model-variant fallback path validated (int4/int8 -> fp16 fallback)
- End-to-end E2E perf test: 95th percentile latency <120ms on dedicated hardware
- Automated canary deployment and rollback policy in Console
```
Sarah (Infra): Add infra items:
```
- Reserved Dedicated pool provisioned + capacity tests
- VPC peering + on-prem VPN configured and validated
- HSM integration validated in staging with key rotation test
- Network ingress/egress rules + monitoring
```
Lee (Security): And security gating:
```
- Architecture review completed
- Threat model + mitigations documented
- Pen-test scheduled/completed for pilot
- Audit logs enabled (KMS/HSM, auth, model access)
```
Anika (Eng SRE): Ops runbook items:
```
- Alerting: cache drop, latency spikes, high error rate
- Playbook: failover to Hosted + capacity bump path
- Load-test artifact + synthetic traffic runner in CircleCI
```
Maya (Product): This is great. Can folks drop ownership initials next to each bullet and ETA? We need to surface any blockers by EOD tomorrow.
Jonah (Eng Runtime): I'll take Runtime bullets. ETA: prototype quant profile 5d, E2E perf test 9d.
Sarah (Infra): Infra bullets assigned to me. ETA for VPN + Dedicated provision: 7d. HSM staging validation: 6d (needs ops window).
Lee (Security): Security bullets assigned. Architecture review tomorrow 2pm, pen-test request filed, ETA for review docs 3d.
Anika (Eng SRE): I'll own Ops runbook + alerts. ETA 4d for baseline alerts and a Canary config.
Alex (Solutions): I'll assemble acceptance checklist and runbook docs. ETA 3d. I'll also coordinate the customer test window.
Maya (Product): Blockers I can see: guest hardware for on-prem perf, pen-test queue, and HSM procurement window. If any of these slip, we'll propose Hosted fallback for pilot.
Jonah (Eng Runtime): Slight note: fallback behavior needs an explicit contract — will we silently switch to a smaller model or return a 503 with a graceful message? Recommend automatic fallback to Hosted variant with metric tags indicating fallback.
Anika (Eng SRE): +1 to automatic fallback but with throttled traffic to avoid cascading failures. We'll add a circuit-breaker.
Lee (Security): Security caveat: fallback to Hosted requires data-flow approval. If the customer forbids any external routing, fallback won't be allowed. Need explicit customer opt-in in contract.
Maya (Product): Good catch. I'll confirm with the customer and add a checkbox in acceptance: "Fallback to Redwood Hosted allowed for pilot? Y/N".
Alex (Solutions): I'll add that to the onboarding questionnaire and confirm before next Friday.
Maya (Product): OK — plan: owners above, blockers surfaced. Quick sync tomorrow 10:30am to review progress. If anyone can't make it, paste updates here by 10am. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: Note: scheduled Dedicated pool provisioning job queued (job id: 88122). Will post updates to #eng-infra when it starts. :robot_face:
Sarah (Infra): Thanks deploy-bot. I'll watch the job.
Jonah (Eng Runtime): I'll start model conversion and post early perf numbers in the thread.
Maya (Product): Thanks team — appreciate the quick turnaround.
Alex (Solutions): +1. I'll prep the customer checklist and ping legal re: fallback consent.
